They remove one letter, increase actual weight by alpha_i and decrease positive height by one, hence are locally nilpotent. They obey e_i''=psi e_i' psi under the bar. These are equivalently the corresponding primitive-leading-term coefficient maps of the braided half coproduct, with the same twists; the commutator construction fixes which coefficient is e_i' rather than e_i''. (i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and $(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ exists on $U_q^-$, and every normalized homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; by the uniqueness in [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]] there is exactly one such form.
